text: Bond market needs stronger institutional investor base to support growth: VBMA

HÀ NỘI - Việt Nam needs to improve sovereign and corporate credit ratings, expand long-term institutional investment funds and strengthen secondary-market liquidity if its corporate bond market is to play a greater role in financing economic growth, Phạm Phú Khôi, general secretary of the Vietnam Bond Market Association (VBMA), told Việt Nam News reporter Ly Ly Cao.

Following Việt Nam's recent stock market upgrade, could increased international capital inflows help shift the capital market away from its heavy reliance on bank credit towards a greater role for equities and bonds?
How could corporate bonds benefit?
Việt Nam's stock market upgrade is an important milestone, but it applies to the equity market.

For the bond market to achieve significant growth in both quality and scale, Việt Nam needs to secure an upgrade in its sovereign credit rating, which would also help improve corporate issuers' credit ratings.

Restructuring the debt capital market requires reducing reliance on bank credit, currently equivalent to around 145 per cent of GDP, while increasing the role of corporate bonds, which account for approximately 11 per cent.
The Government aims to raise the corporate bond market's share to 25 per cent of GDP by 2030.

This requires improving the quality of bond products and credit ratings, developing institutional investors such as bond and pension funds, and increasing secondary-market liquidity through lower transaction fees and coupon taxes.
Việt Nam should also allow the development of bond derivatives and introduce interest rate and foreign exchange hedging instruments to attract foreign investors.
What should Việt Nam do to expand the role of long-term institutional investors, including investment funds, insurers and pension funds?
A strong institutional investor base is essential for sustainable bond market development.
Việt Nam's investment and pension funds have total assets of around VNĐ835 trillion, equivalent to just 6.5 per cent of GDP.
By the end of 2025, the supplementary pension market had only seven funds, with total assets of nearly VNĐ2.21 trillion.
Banks therefore remain the largest investors in corporate bonds.
First, Việt Nam needs to develop long-term funding sources.

Decree 85/2026/ND-CP, effective from May 10, 2026, allows supplementary pension funds to expand their portfolios to listed securities and reduces the minimum allocation to Government bonds to 40 per cent for funds of sufficient size.
More attractive tax incentives and broader participation mechanisms are needed to help pension funds become a major source of long-term capital.
The market also needs products suited to long-term investors, including credit-rated bonds with longer maturities, transparent information and standardised structures.
Decree 200/2026/ND-CP and Circular 138/2026/TT-BTC provide a basis for improving the quality of privately placed corporate bonds.
Public offerings, green bonds and infrastructure bonds should also be encouraged.

Third, market infrastructure must be strengthened to improve secondary-market liquidity, reduce transaction costs and coupon income taxes, and enable foreign investors to hedge currency and interest rate risks.
Independent bond valuation organisations and intermediary brokers are also needed to support liquidity and establish a reliable benchmark yield curve.
The objective is not to reduce banks' role, but to distribute risks more appropriately so that short-term capital does not have to finance long-term investment needs.
How much can the bond market contribute to Việt Nam's growing capital needs, and what conditions are necessary to reduce reliance on bank credit?
Total social investment capital required for 2026-2030 is estimated at around VNĐ38.5 quadrillion, averaging VNĐ7.7 quadrillion annually, or about 40 per cent of GDP.
The domestic and foreign private sectors are expected to contribute around VNĐ25.5 quadrillion, equivalent to 65 per cent of the total.
The Securities Market Development Strategy to 2030 targets total outstanding bond market debt of at least 58 per cent of GDP, including corporate bonds at 25 per cent.
However, the total bond market reached only around VNĐ3.7 quadrillion, or 32.1 per cent of GDP, in 2025.
Corporate bond outstanding debt stood at approximately VNĐ1.48 quadrillion, equivalent to 10.9 per cent of GDP, at the end of the second quarter of 2026.
Government bonds are the main channel for financing public investment and establishing a benchmark yield curve.
Corporate bonds, including infrastructure, project and green bonds, can provide long-term funding for private sector projects with extended payback periods.

To fulfil this role, the market needs transparent issuers, clear use of proceeds and debt repayment plans, broader credit rating coverage, stronger long-term institutional investors and more liquid secondary trading.
Domestic funding alone will not be sufficient to meet the projected investment needs, so foreign capital must also be considered.
Foreign investors have so far had very limited participation in the domestic corporate bond market.
Việt Nam needs to secure an investment-grade sovereign credit rating and introduce coordinated measures to attract overseas investors. - BIZHUB/VNS
